topic.subject: science
topic.title: Coal and petroleum
topic.scope: fossil fuels formation, coal products, petroleum refining, natural gas, conserving fuels

misconceptions.statement: Sunlight is an exhaustible resource because everything on Earth eventually runs out.
misconceptions.why: Students overgeneralize the concept of scarcity to all natural resources.
misconceptions.fix: Sunlight and wind are inexhaustible because they are not significantly depleted by human consumption and are constantly renewed.

probe.question: If we build millions of solar panels, will the sun's energy reach a limit for us?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, we will use up the sun's light eventually.

misconceptions.root_belief: all resources are finite and can be used up

misconceptions.statement: Coal is formed from the remains of dead dinosaurs and large animals.
misconceptions.why: The term 'fossil' is strongly associated with dinosaurs in popular media.
misconceptions.fix: Coal is formed specifically from the remains of dense vegetation and forests buried under the earth millions of years ago.

probe.question: What was the primary source material for the coal found in mines today?

misconceptions.root_belief: fossils only refer to animal remains

misconceptions.statement: Fossil fuels can be recreated in a laboratory in a few days if we have the right heat and pressure.
misconceptions.why: Students underestimate the geological time scale required for these processes.
misconceptions.fix: The formation of fossil fuels takes millions of years; even with high heat and pressure, the biological and chemical transformation cannot be rushed.

probe.question: Why can't we just make more coal in factories to solve the energy crisis?
probe.wrong_answer: We just don't have the right machines yet, but it's a fast process.

misconceptions.root_belief: human technology can replicate any natural process quickly

misconceptions.statement: Coke used in industry is the same as the soft drink Coca-Cola.
misconceptions.why: The identical name leads to linguistic confusion.
misconceptions.fix: Coke is a tough, porous, and black substance which is an almost pure form of carbon, used in the manufacture of steel.

probe.question: What is the physical state and use of 'coke' in a steel plant?
probe.wrong_answer: It is a liquid drink used to cool the machines.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word has only one everyday meaning

misconceptions.statement: Petroleum and Petrol are exactly the same thing.
misconceptions.why: In many Indian contexts, the terms are used interchangeably in daily speech.
misconceptions.fix: Petroleum is the raw crude oil, while petrol is just one of the many constituents obtained after refining petroleum.

probe.question: Is the liquid pumped out from deep under the sea directly called petrol?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, petrol is found in underground pools.

misconceptions.root_belief: the name of a part represents the whole
misconceptions.source_hint: Common diagnostic errors in Indian chemistry classrooms

misconceptions.statement: Refining petroleum means filtering out dirt and sand from the oil.
misconceptions.why: The word 'refining' or 'purifying' usually implies removing unwanted impurities like dust.
misconceptions.fix: Refining is the process of separating the various constituents or fractions of petroleum based on their different boiling points.

probe.question: What happens inside a petroleum refinery?
probe.wrong_answer: They wash the oil to remove mud and stones.

misconceptions.root_belief: refining means cleaning or removing dirt

misconceptions.statement: Paraffin wax is obtained from plants or bees, not from petroleum.
misconceptions.why: Wax is traditionally associated with biological sources like honeycombs.
misconceptions.fix: Paraffin wax is a byproduct of petroleum refining and is used in making candles and ointments.

probe.question: Which of these is a constituent of petroleum: Wood, Paraffin Wax, or Sand?
probe.wrong_answer: Wood, because wax comes from bees.

misconceptions.root_belief: materials with similar properties must have similar origins

misconceptions.statement: CNG and LPG are the same gas used for the same purposes.
misconceptions.why: Both are gases used as fuel and have three-letter acronyms.
misconceptions.fix: CNG (Compressed Natural Gas) is mainly methane used in vehicles, while LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) is a petroleum product used mainly for cooking.

probe.question: Can we use the gas from our kitchen cylinder (LPG) to run a CNG car directly?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, they are both just natural gas.

misconceptions.statement: Petroleum is found in large hollow caves or lakes deep underground.
misconceptions.why: Diagrams in textbooks often show oil 'pockets' which students interpret as open swimming pools of oil.
misconceptions.fix: Petroleum is actually trapped within the tiny pores of sedimentary rocks, much like water in a sponge.

probe.question: If you went deep underground to an oil source, what would you see?
probe.wrong_answer: A large underground lake of black liquid.

misconceptions.root_belief: liquids underground must exist in large open containers
misconceptions.source_hint: Rosalind Driver's Children's Ideas in Science

misconceptions.statement: We don't need to conserve fossil fuels because new ones are being formed every day.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the 'process' of formation with the 'rate' of formation.
misconceptions.fix: While formation is a continuous process, it takes millions of years, making the rate of formation negligible compared to our rate of consumption.

probe.question: Why is coal considered a non-renewable resource if it is still forming underground?
probe.wrong_answer: It is actually renewable because it never stops forming.

misconceptions.statement: Coal tar is only used for surfacing roads.
misconceptions.why: This is the most visible and common everyday use students observe.
misconceptions.fix: Coal tar is a starting material for many products like synthetic dyes, drugs, perfumes, and even naphthalene balls.

probe.question: Where else might the chemicals from coal tar be found besides roads?
probe.wrong_answer: Nowhere else, it is only for road construction.

misconceptions.root_belief: an object has only its most visible use

misconceptions.statement: All products obtained from petroleum are liquids.
misconceptions.why: Petroleum itself is a liquid, so students assume its 'parts' must be liquids too.
misconceptions.fix: Petroleum refining produces gases (LPG), liquids (Petrol, Diesel), and solids/semi-solids (Paraffin wax, Bitumen).

probe.question: Is bitumen, used for roads, a liquid like petrol?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, all petroleum products must be liquid to flow through pipes.

misconceptions.root_belief: properties of the whole apply to all parts
